newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says city employees not protected under transfer rules.
newsitem.headline: Court says city employees not protected under transfer rules.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday municipal administration employees are not covered by Community rules designed to secure employment after business mergers or transfers.

Annette Henke, a secretary in the mayor's office in Schierke, Germany, was laid off after the administrative functions of the city were handed over to a newly formed administrative collectivity, or regional authority.

Henke argued that under German law her contract of employment had been transferred to the new regional authority and therefore could not be terminated. The German law in question implements Community rules protecting employees in the event of transfers of business undertakings.

The European Commission submitted an opinion to the court that the directive's meaning of "undertaking" does not extend to public entities. Britain offered the opinion that a local public authority does not come within the scope of the directive if it mainly or solely performs activities typical of those carried out by a public service. Germany argued that municipalities are not undertakings because they do not carry out any economic activity.
The court found the member state arguments persuasive and supported by the different language versions of the directive designating the subject of the transfer and the beneficary of the transfer.
The court said that the purpose of the integration of different municipalities' administrative tasks was not of an economic nature, and not covered by the directive.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: German)

Safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings - Transfer of certain administrative functions of a municipality to a body created for that purpose by several municipalities"
Reference by the Arbeitsgericht Halberstadt (Germany) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of article 1(1) of Council directive 77/187/EEC of 14 February 1977 on the approximation of the laws of the members states relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses (OJ 1977 L 61, p. 26)

Article 1(1) of Council directive 77/187/EEC of 14 February 1977 on the approximation of the laws of the members states relating to the safeguarding of employees' rights in the event of transfers of undertakings, businesses or parts of businesses must be interpreted as meaning that the concept of a "transfer of an undertaking, business or part of a business" does not apply to the transfer of administrative functions from a municipality to an administrative collectivity such as the one in question in the main proceedings.
